Another interesting features of @polyester is Unified Assets.

No matter which network you use to deposit your assets into Polyester, they all become part of a single shared balance.

This means you can use your assets for trading without worrying about which network they came from.

For example, USDT deposited from two different networks enters the same market, so there's no need for separate balances or order books for each network.

Even when withdrawing, you can choose your preferred supported network.

Essentially, you get an experience similar to a centralized exchange but built on decentralized infrastructure!

Imagine an AI agent being able to obtain a license for a song on its own.

Let's walk through how this could work.

Suppose a music producer registers their work in an IP registry and defines the terms under which it can be used.

Now an AI agent wants to use that track in a promotional video.

What happens next?

1. Finding the work and its terms

The agent first discovers information about the track and its licensing terms. For example, whether commercial use is permitted.

2. Checking whether a license can be obtained

This is where "canLicense" comes in.

In simple terms, the agent asks the registry: Is this work available for licensing?

The answer can depend on the conditions and policies defined by that registry.

3. Acquiring and recording an agreement

If the required conditions are met, the agent can use "acquireAgreement" to initiate the licensing agreement process.

Depending on the setup, this step may also involve payment or other checks.

4. Checking the agreement before use

The application preparing to publish the video can then check the status of the recorded agreement to see whether the relevant license is active.

Of course, this technical check does not automatically guarantee that every legal obligation or off-chain condition has been fulfilled.

The interesting part is that the agent isn't simply finding a song. It can interact with a defined system to check licensing information and initiate an agreement.

This is the kind of interaction between intellectual property, licensing and software that ERC-8432 aims to provide a common foundation for.

The first choice in building with @primus_labs is who makes the request the proof is about

For web apps, that's the end user. They create the attestation through the Network-JS-SDK, with the Primus extension in the loop

For backends, it's your server. The Network-Core-SDK needs no extension, but an authorized token is required to request private data

I read these as two kinds of claim: what a user's own session returned and what a server's authorized request returned

The same zkTLS sits underneath, so what changes is whose access the proof came through

Both SDKs run through the Primus Network, the decentralized attestors

Primus also offers zkTLS enterprise solutions and a Lightweight Web SDK for other use cases

Before judging any zkTLS use case, I'd ask whose access the proof was made from

For an institution proving its own numbers, the backend path looks like the natural fit

use this link to access the Primus tasks : https://s.kaito.ai/CvGKi7P

Privacy technology matters most when developers can actually build with it

One thing I find interesting about @primus_labs is that its vision goes beyond proving that private data can be verified

The bigger challenge is making privacy-preserving technology practical for real applications

That's where the developer side becomes important

Primus provides a Developer Hub where builders can explore its tools and start working with its infrastructure

Why does this matter?

🔹 Developers can explore new ways to handle sensitive data

🔹 Privacy-preserving verification can open new possibilities for Web3 applications

🔹 Encrypted computation creates opportunities for applications that don't need direct access to raw user data

I believe privacy shouldn't be limited to a few specialized protocols

It should become something developers can build into everyday applications

The real progress is when privacy becomes a building block, not a limitation

The only thing I have of you is an old photo of the two of us and your memory carved deep in my mind. And patience for my soul to take flight and waiting to see you.

Maybe there's only one thing left I have to do and that was the brilliance you told me about. You told me that when I grew up you'd love to see me in a ballet outfit. Father I'm only alive for this because I promised you and my own dreams.

Artyom this was the last promise I made you. That I'd shine like a star and become a ballerina. The pointe shoes you were going to buy me. Becoming a ballerina and buying those ballet shoes was exactly what the big shoes stole from me in childhood.

Yes I'm going to bear the most pressure and my feet will bear the most weight. New wounds and blisters and calluses and dry skin become a precious gift to me and my body is completed by having all kinds of wounds. But the most beautiful performances always have the deepest pain behind them.

Maybe the worms have eaten the flesh and blood of my body and I'm decomposing. But my bones are still sound. And ballet is my last performance. Like the performance of Natalia Osipova at the Royal Ballet. And the last music I hear is Adagio for Strings by Samuel Barber. Because this performance needs a grand funeral. And stars go out someday too.

Nothing physical is left of the past but my mind is so rich with you. Rich with kindness. Warm soup. Hunting. A bear. A photo of the two of us.

I forgot the last time I smiled and it was probably before you died. Because after that I forgot how to smile. You were the one who taught me when and where to smile and when to frown. But life never gave me the chance for either. All I know is crying and wailing.

Artyom told me to keep a diary for all the time I'm not around and write down every good thing. Forgive me Artyom because this diary has grown so heavy it's going to become a book full of nightmares and traumas and tears and agony.

Whenever something bad happens to me I still repeat under my breath that I'm telling Artyom. But even my lips couldn't bear the weight of this much pain.

There is no salvation for me in life. It comes after my soul takes flight with eternal peace for my soul and body.

By old habit I still take good care of my wounds and let them stay fresh. Yes pus and bloody fluid and filth come out but they describe my soul and body best. Let them stay alive and fresh because they can tell the truth better than my tongue can.

They are my eternal companions in body and mind and soul.
